exposure: Giving birth during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic and associated disease control restrictions
Giving birth before the COVID-19 pandemic
outcome: Maternal mental health (depression, anxiety, social support)
Confidence in caretaking of the newborn
cohort: The study included 90 women who gave birth during the first COVID-19 wave restrictions (16 March - 10 May 2020) and 101 women who gave birth before the pandemic, all surveyed from a single centre in Northern Germany.
finding: Mothers who gave birth under COVID-19 restrictions did not show significant differences in depression, anxiety, social support, birth experience, confidence in caretaking, or perception of neonatal behaviour compared to mothers before the pandemic, but they expressed significantly higher dissatisfaction with the maternal role.
cross-section timing: Data was assessed at 3-8 weeks postpartum for both groups.
